newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders say shipping delay talk overdone.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders say shipping delay talk overdone.

text.p: Brazilian traders could not confirm talk China was interested in buying South American soybeans but said talk of shipping delays out of Brazil was overdone and any fresh purchases could be promptly shipped.

U.S. traders said China was looking to buy either U.S. or cheaper South American soybeans, but may ultimately plump for the U.S. product because it would be guaranteed prompter shipment than from Latin America.
"There is no delay anymore," said Michael McDougall, director of commodities futures at Fimat Futures. "There is a five-to-seven day wait at Paranagua compared to 25 to 30 days before."
In addition, soybean shipments out of the key southern port of Rio Grande were due to get into swing in May, providing another important outlet for the product, said David Brew, trader at Brasoja.

"It's not so difficult to get beans out, you can get them out from Rio Grande," said Brew, adding that it was always possible to find someone willing to cede an earlier shipment if the price was right.
"You can always find someone who says, 'Alright, you can have mine, I'll ship a little later'," he said.
Officials at Paranagua port were not able to give an estimate of waiting time for ships loading soybeans and soy products.
On Tuesday, there was one vessel loading 55,000 tonnes soybeans, three vessels loading a total of 94,600 tonnes soymeal and one vessel loading 15,500 tonnes mixed cargo.
Nine vessels were waiting to dock to load soymeal, six for soybeans and two for mixed cargo.

"The number of vessels waiting to dock is dropping, loading is much faster now," said a port spokeswoman, adding that she expected loading to decrease now with the harvest practically 100 percent completed in Parana state.
Officials at Rio Grande were also unable to give an estimated waiting time, saying that it varied from vessel to vessel.
On Tuesday, the Polska Walczaca was loading 57,250 tonnes soybeans, the Dunaj 18,333 tonnes soymeal and the Evgenia 53,000 tonnes soymeal.
Seven vessels were expected to arrive until May 12 to load a total of 143,650 tonnes soybeans and 80,000 tonnes soymeal.
